name: Mauritania
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: Ghana Empire dominates the trade routes
claims.summary: The Soninke kingdom of Ghana (Wagadou) controls the trans-Saharan gold-and-salt trade, with its influence reaching into the south of present-day Mauritania.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-700-ghana-empire-dominates-the-trade-routes, claim TL:MRT:event:700:ghana-empire-dominates-the-trade-routes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Koumbi Saleh as a Saharan emporium
claims.summary: Koumbi Saleh, widely identified as Ghana's capital, grows into a major trading town with a Muslim merchants' quarter and, at its peak, tens of thousands of inhabitants.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-800-koumbi-saleh-as-a-saharan-emporium, claim TL:MRT:event:800:koumbi-saleh-as-a-saharan-emporium, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Break-up of the Sanhaja confederation
claims.summary: The confederation of veiled Sanhaja Berbers controlling the western Saharan trade routes fragments, producing warfare and unrest among the desert tribes.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1000-break-up-of-the-sanhaja-confederation, claim TL:MRT:event:1000:break-up-of-the-sanhaja-confederation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abdallah ibn Yasin founds the Almoravid movement
claims.summary: The theologian Abdallah ibn Yasin begins preaching a reformed Islam among the Sanhaja, gathering the disciplined religious-military following known as the al-Murabitun (Almoravids).
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1040-abdallah-ibn-yasin-founds-the-almoravid-movement, claim TL:MRT:event:1040:abdallah-ibn-yasin-founds-the-almoravid-movement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Ibn Yasin; Abu Bakr leads the desert wing
claims.summary: After Ibn Yasin is killed in 1059, Abu Bakr ibn Umar takes command of the Almoravid forces in the Sahara, while Yusuf ibn Tashfin leads the northern conquests.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1059-death-of-ibn-yasin-abu-bakr-leads-the-desert, claim TL:MRT:event:1059:death-of-ibn-yasin-abu-bakr-leads-the-desert, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Almoravids said to take Koumbi Saleh
claims.summary: Tradition records that Almoravid forces under Abu Bakr captured the Ghanaian capital of Koumbi Saleh around 1076, contributing to the decline of the Ghana Empire—though the campaign's scale is debated.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1076-almoravids-said-to-take-koumbi-saleh, claim TL:MRT:event:1076:almoravids-said-to-take-koumbi-saleh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of the Almoravid empire
claims.summary: The Almoravid empire, which had stretched from the Senegal River to Spain, is overthrown by the Almohads, but Islam remains firmly rooted in the western Sahara.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1147-fall-of-the-almoravid-empire, claim TL:MRT:event:1147:fall-of-the-almoravid-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Beni Hassan Arab migration
claims.summary: Waves of Banu Maqil Arabs, including the Beni Hassan, migrate south into the western Sahara, spreading Hassaniya Arabic and gradually transforming the region's Berber society.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1200-beni-hassan-arab-migration, claim TL:MRT:event:1200:beni-hassan-arab-migration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of the caravan ksour
claims.summary: The fortified towns of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata are founded to serve the trans-Saharan caravans, becoming trading and religious centres of Islamic culture.

sources.label: Ancient Ksour of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata
Ancient Ksour of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1100-foundation-of-the-caravan-ksour, claim TL:MRT:event:1100:foundation-of-the-caravan-ksour, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Char Bouba (Marabout) war
claims.summary: Sanhaja Berber religious leaders fight the Arab Beni Hassan tribes; the war's outcome confirms Arab warrior dominance and the social hierarchy of Moorish society.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1644-the-char-bouba-marabout-war, claim TL:MRT:event:1644:the-char-bouba-marabout-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Moorish emirates
claims.summary: Moorish society consolidates into the emirates of Trarza, Brakna, Tagant and Adrar, each governed by an emir of the Hassan warrior elite.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1680-rise-of-the-moorish-emirates, claim TL:MRT:event:1680:rise-of-the-moorish-emirates, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coppolani's pacification campaign begins
claims.summary: Xavier Coppolani launches France's drive to extend control over Mauritania, combining alliances with marabout tribes and military pressure on the emirates.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1902-coppolani-s-pacification-campaign-begins, claim TL:MRT:event:1902:coppolani-s-pacification-campaign-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mauritania organised within French West Africa
claims.summary: The territory is formally constituted as the civil territory of Mauritania within French West Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1904-mauritania-organised-within-french-west-africa, claim TL:MRT:event:1904:mauritania-organised-within-french-west-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Coppolani
claims.summary: Xavier Coppolani is killed at Tidjikja, a setback to the French advance, though the conquest of the interior continues afterward.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1905-assassination-of-coppolani, claim TL:MRT:event:1905:assassination-of-coppolani, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Completion of the conquest
claims.summary: After decades of resistance by the desert emirates and nomadic tribes, French military control over the far north of Mauritania is finally consolidated in the 1930s.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1934-completion-of-the-conquest, claim TL:MRT:event:1934:completion-of-the-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Autonomous republic and Nouakchott
claims.summary: Mauritania becomes an autonomous republic within the French Community, and the new capital of Nouakchott is established on the coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1958-autonomous-republic-and-nouakchott, claim TL:MRT:event:1958:autonomous-republic-and-nouakchott, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of the Islamic Republic
claims.summary: Mauritania gains full independence from France; Moktar Ould Daddah leads the new state and becomes its first president in 1961.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-of-the-islamic-republic, claim TL:MRT:event:1960:independence-of-the-islamic-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: National currency and Arab orientation
claims.summary: Mauritania leaves the franc zone and introduces the ouguiya, reflecting Ould Daddah's policy of national consolidation and a turn toward the Arab world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1973-national-currency-and-arab-orientation, claim TL:MRT:event:1973:national-currency-and-arab-orientation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Annexation of southern Western Sahara
claims.summary: Following the 1975 Madrid Accords, Mauritania and Morocco partition Western Sahara; Mauritania annexes the southern third as Tiris al-Gharbiyya, drawing it into war with the Polisario Front.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1976-annexation-of-southern-western-sahara, claim TL:MRT:event:1976:annexation-of-southern-western-sahara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup ends the Daddah era
claims.summary: A military coup deposes President Moktar Ould Daddah after eighteen years in power, as the costly Western Sahara war destabilises the country.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1978-coup-ends-the-daddah-era, claim TL:MRT:event:1978:coup-ends-the-daddah-era, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Withdrawal from Western Sahara
claims.summary: Mauritania renounces its claim to Tiris al-Gharbiyya and withdraws its forces, ending its part in the Western Sahara war; Morocco then absorbs the vacated territory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1979-withdrawal-from-western-sahara, claim TL:MRT:event:1979:withdrawal-from-western-sahara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slavery formally abolished
claims.summary: Mauritania abolishes slavery by decree—frequently cited as the last country in the world to do so—though no penalties were initially attached to the ban.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1981-slavery-formally-abolished, claim TL:MRT:event:1981:slavery-formally-abolished, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ould Taya takes power
claims.summary: Colonel Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya seizes power in a coup and goes on to rule Mauritania for some twenty years.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-1984-ould-taya-takes-power, claim TL:MRT:event:1984:ould-taya-takes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup ends the Taya era
claims.summary: A military council overthrows President Ould Taya, beginning a period of transition punctuated by a further coup in 2008.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-2005-coup-ends-the-taya-era, claim TL:MRT:event:2005:coup-ends-the-taya-era, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slavery criminalised
claims.summary: A law makes slavery a criminal offence; the constitution later recognises it as a crime against humanity in 2012, although rights groups report that descent-based slavery has persisted in practice.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritania: From the Sanhaja desert and the Almoravid jihad to the caravan ksour and the modern Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/MRT/chronicle#ev-2007-slavery-criminalised, claim TL:MRT:event:2007:slavery-criminalised, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
